div.head: III Eg 2
div.ab: ⁊ ne gesece nán man þone cyng for nanre spræce, butan he æt ham rihtes wyrðe beon ne mote oððe riht abiddan ne mæge.
⁊ na geséce nan man þæne cing for nanre spæce, butan he æt ham rihtes wyrþe beon ne móte oððe riht abiddan ne mæge.
⁊ ne gesece nan man þone cyngc for nanre spræce, buton he æt ham rihtes beon ne mote oððe riht abiddan ne mæg.
Et nemo requirat regem pro aliqua causa, nisi domi negetur ei omne dignum recti uel rectum impetrare non possit.
[Be ðone ðe mon cyng gesece ⁊ be ðæm were.] ⁊ ne gesece nan man þone cyngc for nanre spræce, buton he æt ham rihtes [wyrðe] beon ne mote, oððe riht abiddan ne mæg.
And ne gesece nan man þone cyng for nanre spræce butan he æt ham rihtes wyrðe beon ne mote oððe riht abiddan ne mæge.

(Davon, dass jemand den König angeht. Und vom Wergeld. Ld) Und niemand gehe den König an wegen einer Klagesache, ausser wenn er daheim [seines] Rechtes nicht theilhaftig werden kann oder Recht zu erlangen nicht vermag.
(Of applying to the king. And of wergild. Ld) And let no one apply to the king in any suit unless he cannot obtain [his] right at home or cannot get justice.
And no-one shall apply to the king about any case, unless he cannot obtain the benefit of the law or fails to command justice at home.
And no one is to apply to the king in any suit, unless he may not be entitled to right or cannot obtain justice at home.
And no one may petition the king concerning a lawsuit unless he cannot obtain his rights at home and cannot appeal to another court.

note.seg: Be ðone ðe mon cyng gesece; ⁊ be ðæm were Rubrik Ld
Be ðone ðe mon cyng gesece; ⁊ be ðæm were rubric Ld

Vgl. Gl Königsgericht 3; Rechtsweigerung 5a. Der Reichstag, durch des Königs Mund, will gegen zentralisierende Regierungstendenz die Justiz lokal erhalten bei den Magistraten der Provinz und vielleicht im besonderen bei der privaten Gerichtsbarkeit: beide wurden von der Klasse der Magnaten, bisweilen gewiss in Einer Person, ausgenützt.—Obwohl II Cn 17 dies wiederholend nur ‘Rechtes teilhaft werden’ bringt, halt ich das zweite ‘Recht erlangen’, das allein bei As steht, nicht sachlich damit identisch. Wahrscheinlich will jenes die Einlassung in den Prozess, dieses die Urteilserfüllung ausdrücken. Wäre Justizweigerung (s. d. Gl) gemeint, so würde der Gerichtsherr mit Strafe bedroht werden.—Q sieht in wyrðe irrig ein Substantiv

Cf. Gl Königsgericht 3; Rechtsweigerung 5a. The national assembly, through the king’s mouth, seeks, against a centralising tendency of government, to keep justice local, with the magistrates of the province and perhaps in particular with private jurisdiction: both were exploited by the class of magnates, at times no doubt united in a single person. — Although II Cn 17, repeating this, has only ‘become partaker of right’, I do not hold the second phrase, ‘obtain right’, which occurs only in As, to be identical with it in substance. Probably the former is meant to express admission to the suit, the latter the fulfilment of the judgment. If denial of justice (see that word in Gl) were meant, the lord of the court would be threatened with a penalty. — Q wrongly takes wyrðe as a noun

This regulation is repeated in II Cn. 17 but without the second phrase riht abiddan. Liebermann does not consider, however, that the two phrases express the same idea, and suggests that the former refers to ‘die Einlassung in den Prozess,’ the latter to ‘die Urteilserfüllung’ (see iii. p. 136). He suggests further that, if it were a case of justice being refused, a penalty would be inflicted on the official presiding over the local court.
